record.original_question: For associative-commutative unification, do the same or similar transformation rules known to terminate with variable replacement after every step or at the end also terminate under more flexible control strategies?

evidence.quote: Does AC unification terminate under more flexible control?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the problem of associative–commutative (AC) unification: given two first-order terms s and t built from a signature containing one or more binary function symbols declared associative and commutative, find a complete set of substitutions σ such that sσ =_AC tσ, where =_AC denotes equality modulo the associativity and commutativity axioms of those symbols.

Standard AC-unification procedures are presented as nondeterministic transformation systems on systems of equations (e.g., variants of Stickel's algorithm and its refinements). For such transformation systems, termination has been established under restrictive control regimes, namely:
  (a) the strategy that performs a variable-replacement (instantiation) step after every transformation step, and
  (b) the strategy that defers variable replacement until the very end of the derivation.

The problem is to determine whether the same (or analogously formulated) transformation rules for AC-unification still terminate when these rigid control disciplines are loosened, i.e., when variable replacement steps may be interleaved arbitrarily with other transformation steps rather than being constrained to occur after every step or only at the end. Concretely: identify a flexible control strategy strictly more permissive than (a) and (b), and prove that every derivation of the AC-unification transformation system under this strategy is finite; or else exhibit a counterexample showing nontermination.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches surface foundational work on AC-unification termination (Stickel, Fages) and recent formalizations of Stickel-style algorithms in PVS, but none of the located sources directly addresses termination of AC-unification transformation rules under flexible/relaxed control strategies in the sense posed here. The current status of this specific question could not be verified from the available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Unification theory (Snyder)
status_evidence.snippet: Stickel's proof of termination did not apply to the general case; Fages later proposed a measure to fix the termination proof.
status_evidence.claim: Termination of AC-unification has historically been delicate and tied to specific control disciplines.

status_evidence.title: A Certified Algorithm for AC-Unification
status_evidence.snippet: First formalization of termination, soundness and completeness of an AC-unification algorithm (a modified Stickel algorithm) in PVS.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work formalizes termination for specific AC-unification algorithms but does not settle termination under arbitrary flexible control.
